candidates.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI deep learning model combined with clinical model for noninvasive differentiation of hepatocellular carcinoma from mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma
candidates.abstract: Rationale and objectives This study aims to develop a framework integrating dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI)-based multi-channel deep learning combined with clinical modeling for the non-invasive preoperative discrimination between hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and mass-forming intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (MF-ICC). Methods The internal development cohort comprised 334 surgically confirmed patients, including 231 patients with HCC and 103 with MF-ICC, and was divided at the patient level into a training cohort ( n = 233) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 101). The independent external validation cohort included 50 patients, comprising 40 with HCC and 10 with MF-ICC. We constructed separate two-dimensional deep learning models based on arterial phase, portal venous phase, and delayed phase images and then developed fusion models (2D model). A multi-channel deep learning model was further developed by directly inputting the three-phase images stacked along the channel dimension. Moreover, a clinical model was built based on independent predictors identified through multivariate analysis, which was ultimately integrated with the best-performing deep learning model. Model performance was evaluated and compared. Results Deep learning model directly feeding the three-phase images as a multi-channel input achieved better discrimination (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.814 in the internal validation cohort) than all single-phase and corresponding fusion models. The comprehensive 2D + multi-channel + clinical model showed the best performance for the differentiation of HCC from MF-ICC, achieving an AUC of 0.887 (95% CI, 0.819–0.954) in the internal validation cohort, and generalized well to the external validation cohort (AUC = 0.908; 95% CI, 0.811–1.000). However, no significant differences in AUCs were found among the models after correction for multiple comparisons. Conclusion The fusion model integrating clinical predictors with DCE-MRI multi-phase deep learning feature may provide a valuable tool for preoperatively differentiating HCC from MF-ICC.

candidates.title: LIVER CANCER DETECTION USING RESNET, SWIN TRANSFORMER AND CONVNEXT TINY NETWORKS
candidates.abstract: Liver tumor detection from CT images is challenging because most CT slices do not contain tumors, while only a small number contain tumor regions. Another challenge is that slices from the same patient can be very similar, which may cause data leakage when splitting the data randomly. This study focuses on classifying liver CT slices into Tumor and No-Tumor classes using deep learning. The LiTS and 3Dircadb datasets are combined and used for the experiments. Three deep learning models, Swin-T, ConvNeXt-Tiny, and ResNet-50, are trained and evaluated. A patient-level data split is used to keep patients in the training, validation, and test sets separate. The three models are also combined using a soft-voting ensemble. The final evaluation is performed on an unseen test set containing 6,323 slices. The soft-voting ensemble achieved the highest accuracy of 92.74%. These results show that the models can detect tumor and no-tumor slices, while the class imbalance remains an important challenge for tumor detection.

candidates.title: Preoperative prediction of HCC microvascular invasion by multimodel peritumoral diffusion MRI
candidates.abstract: Abstract Objective Most studies emphasize intratumoral diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) metrics, but few studies have examined whether peritumoral DWI metrics can provide added value. We aimed to evaluate three-dimensional, multiscale, multimodel DWI parameters within intratumoral and peritumoral volumes of interest for predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Materials and methods Seventy patients with HCC, including 42 with MVI, were prospectively enrolled. We calculated parameters from monoexponential, intravoxel incoherent motion, diffusion kurtosis imaging (DKI), stretched-exponential model (SEM), and continuous-time random-walk models within the tumor and in 3-mm (P3) and 5-mm (P5) peritumoral rims. Features showing differences on univariable analysis were further screened using logistic regression with variance inflation factor filtering to build combined models. Diagnostic performance was assessed by areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC). Results Four intratumoral diffusion-coefficient–related metrics showed significant differences between groups. In the peritumoral regions, 12 parameters differed between groups, including diffusion-coefficient–related indices and heterogeneity-related metrics. Among single parameters, P3_DKI_ K app achieved the best discrimination for MVI (AUROC = 0.713); P5_DKI_ K app and Tumor_SEM_DDC were selected as independent imaging predictors. After integrating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) and tumor size, the combined model (Cli-IntraPeriDWI) yielded the best performance (AUROC = 0.844). SHAP analysis indicated that higher AFP, larger tumor size, higher P5_DKI_ K app , and lower Tumor_SEM_DDC were associated with increased MVI risk. Conclusion Peritumoral DWI offers multiple biomarkers and outperforms intratumoral metrics for MVI prediction. An interpretable model integrating peritumoral and intratumoral DWI with clinical factors enables accurate, noninvasive preoperative MVI risk stratification in HCC. Key Points Question Can multiscale, multimodel peritumoral DWI metrics improve preoperative prediction of MVI in HCC compared with intratumoral DWI metrics? Findings Compared with intratumoral DWI, peritumoral DWI offered more potential imaging biomarkers and superior diagnostic capability for the preoperative diagnosis of MVI in HCC. Relevance statement By integrating intratumoral and peritumoral metrics with clinical risk factors, we developed a model achieving optimal performance and transparent decision interpretability for MVI assessment, supporting preoperative prognostic evaluation and individualized treatment planning in HCC.

candidates.title: Preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion in small hepatocellular carcinoma (≤ 3 cm) by leveraging cross-phase variations of MRI contrast phases
candidates.abstract: Abstract Purpose Noninvasive preoperative prediction of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a significant clinical challenge worldwide. This study encoded feature variations across multi-phase MRI sequences for the preoperative prediction of MVI. Method Data were retrospectively examined for 115 consecutive patients (mean age: 57.2 ± 10.7 years; 95 men) who had undergone surgical resection for HCC (tumor diameter less than 3 cm). All of them underwent preoperative MR examination and were randomly partitioned into training and testing cohorts at an 8:2 ratio. Peritumoral expansions (3 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm) were generated from manually segmented intratumoral regions of interest (ROIs) across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases. Radiomics features were subsequently extracted from both the original and expanded ROIs. We then evaluated the predictive performance of five encoding methods combined with four machine learning classifiers using both clinical characteristics and radiomics features. Result Multi-phase models incorporating temporal encoding methods consistently outperformed single-phase models and those relying solely on clinical characteristics. Among all evaluated combinations, the Fourier-inspired temporal encoding method combined with an ExtraTrees classifier, applied to the original tumoral ROI with a 5-mm peritumoral expansion, achieved the best diagnostic performance, with an AUC of 0.850 (95% CI: 0.675–0.978). Conclusion While radiologists routinely monitor multi-phase contrast dynamics qualitatively, our findings demonstrate that these cross-phase variations provide quantifiable, highly predictive information for MVI. This framework represents a promising, noninvasive quantitative tool for preoperative MVI risk stratification.

candidates.title: A multiparametric liver MRI dataset with multiple tumor and liver segmentations of pre-treatment hepatocellular carcinomas
candidates.abstract: Abstract Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is the most common primary liver cancer and a leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. While dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) plays a key role for HCC screening, diagnosis and treatment planning, the development of AI models for detection and characterization of focal liver lesions is hindered by the scarcity of publicly available annotated MRI datasets. Here, we present OpenSwissHCC, a curated multiphasic dataset of 132 multiparametric DCE-MRI scans from adult patients with chronic liver disease acquired on 1.5 T and 3 T MRI scanners between 2011 and 2020. The dataset includes both HCC-positive (n = 63) and HCC-negative (n = 69) patients, with up to five lesions per patient segmented across each sequence when confidently identified. Whole-liver and lesion segmentations were manually performed and expert-validated, with lesion metadata including LI-RADS scores, size, liver segment location, major LI-RADS imaging features (non-rim APHE, washout, capsule, threshold growth) and key ancillary/background findings (e.g., mosaic architecture, fat/blood products, necrosis, tumor-in-vein; cirrhosis and portal-hypertension signs). In total, 140 lesions were annotated, including 97 confirmed HCC. Additionally, we provide liver masks for all T1-weighted images (T1-WI) sequences, generated using a pre-trained nnU-Net model, as well as pre-computed transforms to facilitate registration across T1-WI phases. By providing a comprehensive, well-annotated, and standardized collection of liver MRI examinations, OpenSwissHCC aims to assist the development and benchmarking of advanced computational methods for automated HCC detection, segmentation, and characterization, fostering progress toward precision imaging and personalized treatment planning.

candidates.title: Multiparametric MRI-based radiomics combined with deep learning for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma
candidates.abstract: Objective To develop and compare radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models based on multiparametric MRI radiomics and 2.5D deep learning features for preoperative risk stratification of endometrial carcinoma (EC). Methods This retrospective study included 246 patients with pathologically confirmed EC, with preoperative clinical and imaging data collected. Clinical data, T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI) were collected. Radiomics and deep learning models were constructed based on T2WI, CE-T1WI, and their combination. A combined model integrating multiparametric radiomics features, deep learning features, and clinical parameters was subsequently developed. Model performance and clinical utility were evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), and the DeLong test for pairwise model comparisons. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was employed to enhance model interpretability. Results Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis identified maximum tumor diameter, MR-DMI, BMI and ER status as independent predictive factors. Comparison of radiomics, deep learning, clinical, and combined models demonstrated that the multiparametric MRI model outperformed single-sequence models based on radiomics or deep learning, while the combined model exhibited the best predictive performance in the validation set, achieving an AUC of 0.891, accuracy of 0.86, sensitivity of 0.909, specificity of 0.765, and F1-score of 0.896. DeLong test results showed that, in the training set, the combined model had higher predictive performance than all other models, and the differences were statistically significant (P < 0.05). In the validation set, the combined model showed statistically significant improvements compared with the clinical model and the T2+CET1-Rad model (P<0.05). Decision curve analysis indicated that the combined model provided the highest clinical net benefit. Conclusion The combination of multiparametric MRI-based radiomics and 2.5D deep learning demonstrated favorable predictive performance in stratifying risk for EC, suggesting its potential utility as a non-invasive tool and offering a promising adjunctive approach to support personalized treatment planning and prognostic evaluation for EC patients in clinical practice.

candidates.title: Varying diffusion curvature, intravoxel incoherent motion, and conventional monoexponential diffusion models for evaluating Ki-67 expression in rectal carcinoma
candidates.abstract: Objectives This study aimed to systematically evaluate and compare the diagnostic performance of three diffusion models — varying diffusion curvature (VDC), intravoxel incoherent motion (IVIM), and conventional monoexponential diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) — in predicting Ki-67 expression status in rectal adenocarcinoma. Methods A total of 84 patients with rectal carcinoma were enrolled, comprising 48 cases with high proliferative activity (Ki-67 > 50%) and 36 cases with low proliferative activity (Ki-67 ≤ 50%). All patients underwent pelvic MRI examinations. The following imaging parameters were calculated and compared: VDC-derived parameters (D 0 , D 1 ), IVIM-derived parameters (ADC slow , ADC fast , f), and the DWI-derived parameter (ADC). Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify independent predictive factors, and diagnostic performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), the DeLong test, and calibration curves. Results Compared with the low-proliferation group, the high-proliferation group of rectal carcinoma exhibited significantly higher D 1 and f values, along with markedly lower D 0 , ADC, and ADC slow values (all P < 0.05). Logistic regression analysis identified D 1 and ADC slow as independent predictors of Ki-67 status in rectal carcinoma. The combined diagnostic model incorporating D 1 and ADC slow yielded an AUC of 0.924, which was significantly superior to the individual parameters, including ADC (AUC = 0.780), ADC slow (AUC = 0.832), D 0 (AUC = 0.696), D 1 (AUC = 0.857), and f (AUC = 0.802) (all P < 0.05). The calibration curve demonstrated good stability and reliability of the combined diagnostic model. Conclusion Both VDC, IVIM, and DWI demonstrate efficacy in evaluating the Ki-67 expression status in rectal carcinoma. The combined parameters of D 1 and ADC slow may serve as a novel and reliable imaging biomarker for assessing the proliferative activity of rectal carcinoma.

candidates.title: Radiomics of Preoperative Multi-Sequence Magnetic Resonance Imaging Can Improve the Predictive Performance of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
candidates.abstract: Background: The aim of the study is to demonstrate that radiomics of preoperative multi-sequence magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can indeed improve the predictive performance of microvascular invasion (MVI) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Methods: A total of 206 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC who underwent preoperative enhanced MRI were retrospectively recruited. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analysis identified the independent clinicoradiologic predictors of MVI present and constituted the clinicoradiologic model. Recursive feature elimination (RFE) was applied to select radiomics features (extracted from six sequence images) and constructed the radiomics model. Clinicoradiologic model plus radiomics model formed the clinicoradiomics model. Five-fold cross-validation was used to validate the three models. Discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility were used to evaluate the performance. Net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to compare the prediction accuracy between models. Results: The clinicoradiologic model contained alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)_lg10, radiological capsule enhancement, enhancement pattern and arterial peritumoral enhancement, which were independent risk factors of MVI. There were 18 radiomics features related to MVI constructed the radiomics model. The mean area under the receiver operating curve (AUC) of clinicoradiologic, radiomics and clinicoradiomics model were 0.849, 0.925 and 0.950 in the training cohort and 0.846, 0.907 and 0.933 in the validation cohort, respectively. The three models' calibration curves fitted well, and decision curve analysis (DCA) confirmed the clinical usefulness. Compared with the clinicoradiologic model, the NRI of radiomics and clinicoradiomics model increased significantly by 0.575 and 0.825, respectively, and the IDI increased significantly by 0.280 and 0.398, respectively. Conclusions: Radiomics of preoperative multi-sequence MRI can improve the predictive performance of MVI in HCC.

candidates.title: Application of texture signatures based on multiparameter-magnetic resonance imaging for predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma: Retrospective study
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite continuous changes in treatment methods, the survival rate for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) patients remains low, highlighting the importance of diagnostic methods for HCC. AIM: To explore the efficacy of texture analysis based on multi-parametric magnetic resonance (MR) imaging (MRI) in predicting microvascular invasion (MVI) in preoperative HCC. METHODS: This study included 105 patients with pathologically confirmed HCC, categorized into MVI-positive and MVI-negative groups. We employed Original Data Analysis, Principal Component Analysis, Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA), and Non-LDA (NDA) for texture analysis using multi-parametric MR images to predict preoperative MVI. The effectiveness of texture analysis was determined using the B11 program of the MaZda4.6 software, with results expressed as the misjudgment rate (MCR). RESULTS: Texture analysis using multi-parametric MRI, particularly the MI + PA + F dimensionality reduction method combined with NDA discrimination, demonstrated the most effective prediction of MVI in HCC. Prediction accuracy in the pulse and equilibrium phases was 83.81%. MCRs for the combination of T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), arterial phase, portal venous phase, and equilibrium phase were 22.86%, 16.19%, 20.95%, and 20.95%, respectively. The area under the curve for predicting MVI positivity was 0.844, with a sensitivity of 77.19% and specificity of 91.67%. CONCLUSION: Texture analysis of arterial phase images demonstrated superior predictive efficacy for MVI in HCC compared to T2WI, portal venous, and equilibrium phases. This study provides an objective, non-invasive method for preoperative prediction of MVI, offering a theoretical foundation for the selection of clinical therapy.
